title: Soft kernels give lifting over closed subsets and soft quotients
statement: Let $X$ be a paracompact Hausdorff topological space, meaning that every open cover has a locally finite open refinement, and let $0\to A\to B\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ be a short exact sequence in the abelian category of sheaves of abelian groups on its open-subset site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For a closed subset $S\subseteq X$ write $F|_S=i_S^{-1}F$, where $i_S:S\hookrightarrow X$ is inclusion with the subspace topology: sections of $F|_S$ are families of germs of $F$ along $S$ locally represented by sections on open subsets of $X$. Call $F$ soft if $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(S,F|_S)$ is surjective for every closed $S\subseteq X$. If $A$ is soft, then $\Gamma(S,B|_S)\xrightarrow{p|_S}\Gamma(S,C|_S)$ is surjective for every closed $S\subseteq X$, including $S=X$. If $A$ and $B$ are soft, then $C$ is soft.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf. IV §4, Proposition (4.14), printed p.205, with Definition (4.9) and the standing paracompact Hausdorff hypothesis of §4.B.

proof.text: Write $j:A\to B$ for the first arrow. Fix a closed $S\subseteq X$ and $c\in\Gamma(S,C|_S)$. The case $S=\varnothing$ has its unique lift, so assume otherwise. By [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-short-exact-stalkwise], $0\to A_x\xrightarrow{j_x}B_x\xrightarrow{p_x}C_x\to0$ is exact for every $x$. At each $x\in S$ choose a germ $b_x\in B_x$ with $p_x(b_x)=c_x$. Represent $c$ and $b_x$ by ambient sections near $x$. Equality of their image germs lets us shrink to an open $O_x$ on which the representatives have the same image. Thus there is $h_x\in B(O_x)$ with $p(h_x)|_{S\cap O_x}=c|_{S\cap O_x}$. Only this local lifting, not surjectivity of sections on an arbitrary open, has been used.

source.place: Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian; sheaves.tex Section 007S (section-exactness-points); Demailly IV (4.14), local lifting as in (4.3)

proof.text: The opens $O_x$ together with $X\setminus S$ cover $X$. By the defining paracompactness assumption choose a locally finite open refinement $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ covering $X$, and assign to each $U_i$ an original cover member containing it. If that member is $O_x$, restrict $h_x$ to obtain $h_i\in B(U_i)$; if it is $X\setminus S$, take $h_i=0$. The cover $(U_i)$ is point-finite: a point has an open neighborhood meeting only finitely many $U_i$, so it lies in only finitely many. Apply [lem-sfb-paracompact-point-finite-shrinking] to the closed subset $X$ of $X$ and the open cover $(U_i)$: there are opens $V_i$ with $\bigcup_iV_i=X$ and $\overline{V_i}\subseteq U_i$. Put $K_i=\overline{V_i}$, closed in $X$, so $K_i\subseteq U_i$ and $\bigcup_iK_i=X$. Put $D_i=S\cap K_i$ and $b_i=h_i|_{D_i}$. Then $p(b_i)=c|_{D_i}$. The $D_i$ cover $S$ and form a locally finite family of closed subsets of $X$, since $D_i\subseteq U_i$.

source.place: Demailly IV §4.B, Proposition (4.14), printed p.205; details of the closed-cover induction indicated there and in Proposition (4.13), printed p.204

proof.text: The elementary pasting fact needed below follows directly from locally represented germs. For any locally finite family of closed sets $(E_i)$, every subfamily union $E_J$ is closed: near a point outside it, only finitely many $E_i$ occur, and their closedness lets us avoid all of them. Compatible sections along the $E_i$ give a well-defined germ family on their union. At a point $x$ of the union, take a neighborhood meeting finitely many $E_i$, discard those not containing $x$ by shrinking, and choose ambient representatives near $x$ for the finitely many remaining sections. Their germs at $x$ agree, so another finite shrinking makes all these representatives equal. The resulting single representative represents the pasted germ family on the union near $x$. This proves that the pasted family is a section; uniqueness is pointwise equality of germs. The same argument applies to two closed subsets. The open gluing and uniqueness used for representatives are the sheaf condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Demailly IV §4.B, Proposition (4.14), printed p.205; details of the closed-cover induction indicated there and in Proposition (4.13), printed p.204

proof.text: Consider partial lifts $(J,b)$, where $J\subseteq I$, $F_J=\bigcup_{i\in J}D_i$ and $b\in\Gamma(F_J,B|_{F_J})$ satisfies $p(b)=c|_{F_J}$. Order them by extension: $J\subseteq J^{\prime}$ and $b^{\prime}|_{F_J}=b$. The empty partial lift exists. A chain has an upper bound on $J_*=\bigcup J$: for each $i\in J_*$ choose a chain member containing $i$ and restrict its lift to $D_i$. Any two chosen lifts agree wherever both are defined, since the chain members are comparable. Step 3 pastes these compatible sections on the fixed locally finite closed family $(D_i)_{i\in J_*}$; their image is $c$. To apply the subset version [lem-weil-pbc-zorn-lemma], encode $(J,b)$ by $J$ as markers and the graph of its germ family, a subset of $I\sqcup\coprod_{x\in S}B_x$. Inclusion of these codes is precisely the extension order. Thus the cited lemma supplies a maximal partial lift $(J,b)$.

source.place: Demailly IV §4.B, Proposition (4.14), printed p.205; details of the closed-cover induction indicated there and in Proposition (4.13), printed p.204

proof.text: If $i\notin J$, set $T=F_J\cap D_i$, closed in $X$ by Step 3. On $T$ the difference $d=b|_T-b_i|_T$ has image zero under $p$. By the stalk exactness of [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-short-exact-stalkwise], each $d_x$ has a unique preimage $a_x\in A_x$. These preimages are locally represented along $T$: choose an ambient representative $\beta$ of $d$ near $x$ and a representative $\alpha$ of $a_x$; the equality $j_x(a_x)=d_x$ allows shrinking until $j(\alpha)=\beta$. At nearby points of $T$, uniqueness of the kernel preimage identifies the germ of $\alpha$ with the chosen $a_y$. Hence $(a_x)$ is a section $a\in\Gamma(T,A|_T)$. Softness of $A$ gives $\widetilde a\in\Gamma(X,A)$ restricting to $a$. Replace $b_i$ on $D_i$ by $b_i+j(\widetilde a)|_{D_i}$. It still maps to $c$ and now agrees with $b$ on $T$. Step 3 pastes the two sections over $F_J\cup D_i$, giving a strictly larger partial lift because its index set is $J\cup\{i\}$. This contradicts maximality.

source.place: Demailly IV §4.B, Proposition (4.14), printed p.205; details of the closed-cover induction indicated there and in Proposition (4.13), printed p.204

proof.text: Therefore the maximal index set is $I$. Its domain is $F_I=S$, and its section $b$ maps to $c$. This proves the asserted surjectivity for every closed $S$, and in particular for $S=X$, which is closed in itself.

source.place: Demailly IV §4.B, Proposition (4.14), printed p.205; details of the closed-cover induction indicated there and in Proposition (4.13), printed p.204

proof.text: Finally suppose $B$ is also soft. Given a closed $S\subseteq X$ and $c\in\Gamma(S,C|_S)$, Step 6 gives a lift $b\in\Gamma(S,B|_S)$. Extend $b$ to $\widetilde b\in\Gamma(X,B)$ by softness of $B$. The global section $p(\widetilde b)$ restricts to $c$, since a sheaf morphism commutes with restriction of germs. Thus $C$ is soft.

source.place: Demailly IV §4.B, Proposition (4.14), printed p.205; details of the closed-cover induction indicated there and in Proposition (4.13), printed p.204
